cards.text: Jesus has just finished praying in a certain place. One of His disciples walks up with a request. And friend, I LOVE this guy, because he's about to ask what a whole lot of us have been too shy to ask.

cards.question: Jesus just finished praying. What does His disciple ask Him to do?
When he asks, the disciple points out that John the Baptist taught his disciples to pray too. True or false?

cards.text: Yep, John the Baptist had disciples of his own (Luke 7:18-20). So Jesus answers: when you pray, here's what to say.

cards.question: In the prayer Jesus gives His disciples, they open by calling God ___.
Before the prayer Jesus gives asks for anything for the disciples, it starts with God's name and God's kingdom. True or false?

cards.text: Jesus says, "Father, hallowed be Your name. Your kingdom come." Not Dear Sir, not To Whom It May Concern, but FATHER!
Then the prayer comes down from heaven to the kitchen table. Bread.

cards.question: In the prayer, Jesus has His disciples ask God for their bread ___.

cards.text: Next, they ask God to forgive their sins. And right there, the prayer says something about the people praying it.

cards.question: In the prayer, what do the disciples tell God they already do for everyone who sins against them?

cards.text: EVERYONE. Not everyone except the shiny new stamper who took my spot on the counter, and friend, I forgave that guy a long time ago.

cards.question: The prayer Jesus gives ends with one last request. What is it about?

cards.text: Then Jesus tells them a story. Picture this: it's MIDNIGHT, and a man goes to his friend's house to borrow three loaves of bread.

cards.question: The man in Jesus' story needs the bread because a friend of his has come to him on a journey. True or false?

cards.text: And he has nothing to set before his guest. Friend, I know that look: company at the door, cookie jar empty, and you're suddenly VERY interested in the floor.

cards.question: At midnight, what does the friend inside say first to the man asking for bread?
The friend inside says his door is already shut and his children are in bed with him. True or false?

cards.text: He says, "I cannot get up to give you anything." Friend, that is a man who has made peace with his blanket.
Then Jesus tells how it ends. Being friends isn't what gets this man out of bed.

cards.question: In Jesus' story, what does get the friend inside out of bed?

answers.text: A promise to pay him back

cards.question: When the friend inside finally gets up, how much does he give the man?

cards.text: He kept at it at midnight and walked away with all he needed. Friend, that's everybody who ever hit redial on a customer service line until a REAL HUMAN finally picked up.
Then Jesus brings the story home. "So I tell you," He says, and He gives them three things to do.

cards.question: Jesus tells them to ask, seek and knock. What does He say happens when you knock?
Jesus says that everyone who ___ receives.

cards.text: EVERYONE who asks receives. Friend, I spent years where nobody came looking, so that word everyone? I'm gonna need a minute.
Then Jesus asks a question for any father listening. His son asks him for a fish.

cards.question: Jesus asks what father would give his son a ___ instead of the fish he asked for.
In Jesus' next example, the son asks for an egg, and Jesus asks what father would give him a stone instead. True or false?

cards.text: Nope, it's a SCORPION. Fish for a snake, egg for a scorpion, and no father does that, because that's not a gift, that's a jump scare.
Then Jesus lands it. And He's honest about the people He's talking to.

cards.question: Jesus says even people who are evil know how to give good gifts to their children. True or false?
If people who are evil give their children good gifts, what does Jesus say about the Father in heaven?
What does Jesus say the Father in heaven will give to those who ask Him?

cards.text: The Holy Spirit! Friend, I'd have been thrilled with a fresh tub of sprinkles, and He's giving THAT to those who ask Him.

findings.problem: Most choice cards in stop 1 can't be reasoned out from earlier cards. Card 3 (John taught his disciples) has no setup, because card 1 never mentions John. Card 6 (the prayer starts with God's name and kingdom) asks about the prayer's content before any of it is told. Card 9 (bread each day) only has 'Bread.' as setup. Card 13 (the last request is about temptation) has no setup at all. Together with card 5, that makes most of the stop's seven choice cards luck, not informed guesses.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The blank asks for the prayer's opening word ('Father') before any of the prayer has been told, with King and Master as options. This tests wording the baker hasn't seen, not meaning they can reason out. It is like the Psalm 23 'anoint David's head with' example.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This story card only retells Luke 11:2, which cards 5 and 6 already revealed (calling God Father, His name and kingdom). It is a recap and doesn't move the passage forward. The order is also backwards: the choices come before the telling, when the story card should set up the choice.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: This card is only a reaction joke to card 11's answer ('EVERYONE.'). It tells no new part of Luke 11:4, because the temptation line comes on the next card as a choice. The joke has no story beat to ride on.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The answers differ in length and kind. 'The man's persistence' is a short abstract noun phrase. 'A promise to pay him back' and 'Fear of what neighbors think' are longer and more concrete. That makes the right answer stand out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: This card recaps Luke 11:8, which cards 8 and 9 already revealed (persistence, as much as he needs), and then adds a joke. It doesn't move the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: This card restates card 3's answer ('EVERYONE who asks receives') and adds a reaction. It tells no new part of the passage. The next card moves on to Luke 11:11.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: This card restates card 12's answer ('The Holy Spirit!') and adds a joke. It tells nothing new from Luke 11:13 and doesn't move the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.
